subject: Is there a way to reload results of dataProcess and/or groupComparison?

messages.author: ab4c9ed2cd29563b
messages.subject: Is there a way to reload results of dataProcess and/or groupComparison?
parts:
I generally run MSstats inside of R, specifically integrated into Rmarkdown reports.
While working on these reports, I often have to "knit" the document to check the progress. Every knit operation requires re-running the dataProcess and groupComparison steps of MSstats, which are by far the slowest steps.
I was wondering if there is a way to store and quickly reload the results of dataProcess and groupComparison so these can just be read from an object for the purposes of compiling the report.

Thanks,
Jason

messages.author: df9ba0266a9a081f
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to reload results of dataProcess and/or groupComparison?
parts:
I think that you can save the output of dataProcess function or groupComparison function like below and then load them later.

quant <- dataProcess(input)
save(quant, file='quant.rda')

Hope to help.
- Meena

messages.author: ab4c9ed2cd29563b
messages.subject: Re: Is there a way to reload results of dataProcess and/or groupComparison?
parts:
Thanks Meena! Such a simple solution; I should have thought of it earlier.

Here is the code I'm using:
processed.data <- '../Analysis/MSstats.rda'
if(!file.exists(processed.data)){
  rd.proposed <- dataProcess(raw = rd.msstats,
                           normalization = 'equalizeMedians',
                           summaryMethod = 'TMP',
                           censoredInt = "0",
                           cutoffCensored = 'minFeature',
                           MBimpute = TRUE,
                           maxQuantileforCensored = 0.999)
  save(rd.proposed, file=processed.data)
} else {load(processed.data)}

And similarly for the group comparisons:
comparison.data <- '../Analysis/ComparisonResult.rda'
if(!file.exists(comparison.data)){
  baseline.comparisons <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix = comparison, data=rd.proposed)
  save(baseline.comparisons, file=comparison.data)
} else {load(comparison.data)}

Seems to work great!
I realized that it is important to be careful though, especially with the group comparisons. If you change your comparison setup it's critical to go in and delete the saved results so it will regenerate the correct comparisons.
